concerns.text: The plan defines a composite HallucinationIndex (0.5 × (1‑entity_f1) + 0.5 × (1‑semantic_similarity)) but does not describe how the semantic‑similarity component will be validated against human judgments (required by FR‑020). Without this validation the construct validity of the index is questionable.

The manual validation step specifies a stratified random sample ≥ 5 % but does not state which variable(s) the stratification will be based on (e.g., HallucinationIndex, code length, model). Ambiguous stratification can lead to an unrepresentative validation set and bias the calibration of the metric.

Regression and partial‑Spearman analyses control for description length but do not include the model (codegen‑350M vs starcoder‑1b) as a factor. Model‑specific variance could confound the relationship between code characteristics and HallucinationIndex, violating the ‘Code‑Metric Isolation’ principle.

The plan assumes that 1 000 functions provide > 0.8 power to detect a Spearman ρ > 0.1, yet no formal power analysis (effect size, α, β) is presented. Without a documented power calculation the sample may be under‑powered for the intended effect size.
